favorites.name: Chicken Noodle Chilli Gravy
favorites.nutrition:
Calories: ~520 kcal
Protein: 35g
Carbohydrates: 30g
Fat: 25g
Fiber: 4g
Sodium: 650mg
favorites.pairing: Serve with steamed basmati rice or butter naan for a complete meal. A side of sliced onions drizzled with lemon juice, fresh cucumber raita and a wedge of lemon complement the spices beautifully. Finish the meal with a tall glass of chilled salted lassi to balance the heat.
process: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly under cold water, pat completely dry with paper towels and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy-bottomed kadai over medium-high heat until shimmering hot.
Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and wait 20-30 seconds until they splutter and turn golden brown.
Add curry leaves and slit green chillies, fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add finely chopped onions and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the raw smell disappears.
Add pureed tomatoes and cook for 5-6 minutes until the oil starts to separate from the masala.
Lower the heat and add turmeric, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken pieces, increase heat to medium-high and sear for 4-5 minutes, turning to brown all sides.
Add 1 cup noodles and 2 tbsp sause, stir well to combine.
Add 3/4 cup warm water and salt to taste. Stir well to coat chicken and noodles evenly with the masala.
Cover with a tight lid, reduce heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Stir once halfway through.
Uncover, increase heat to medium and cook for 3-4 more minutes to reduce gravy to desired consistency.
Add 1 tsp chilli sause, stir gently and cook for 1 final minute. Turn off the heat.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot with steamed rice or chapati.
tips: Pat chicken completely dry before cooking — any surface moisture prevents proper searing and results in a watery curry.
Fry the onions with patience on medium heat — deeply caramelized golden-brown onions are the biggest secret to a rich, full-bodied curry.
Always add dry spice powders on low heat and stir immediately for 30 seconds — high heat burns the spices and turns the dish bitter.
For a richer, creamier gravy, stir in 2 tbsp fresh cream or thick coconut milk in the final 2 minutes of cooking.
Rest the curry for 5-10 minutes off the heat before serving — the flavors continue to develop and deepen as it sits.

searchHistory.nutrition:
Calories: ~550 kcal
Protein: 20g
Carbohydrates: 60g
Fat: 25g
Fiber: 8g
Sodium: 400mg
searchHistory.pairing: Serve with steamed basmati rice, roti, or naan for a complete meal. A side of sliced cucumbers, carrots, and a dollop of raita complement the spices beautifully. Finish the meal with a tall glass of chilled salted lassi to balance the heat.
process: Soak 1 cup of peanuts in water for 30 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy-bottomed kadai over medium heat until shimmering hot.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and wait 20-30 seconds until they splutter and turn golden brown.
Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and wait 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add curry leaves and slit green chillies, fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add finely chopped onions and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add 3 cloves minced garlic and 1-inch grated ginger, cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the raw smell disappears.
Add 1 cup tamarind paste and cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste thickens.
Add 1 cup soaked peanuts, 1 tsp turmeric powder, 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, and 1 tsp coriander powder. Stir for 1 minute.
Add 2 cups cooked rice and stir well to combine with the peanut mixture.
Add salt to taste and stir well to combine.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors have melded together.
Stir in 0.5 tsp garam masala and cook for 1 final minute.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.
tips: Soak peanuts in water for at least 30 minutes to reduce cooking time and make them easier to digest.
Use a mixture of peanut and vegetable oil for frying to balance the flavor and texture.
Always add tamarind paste on low heat and stir constantly to prevent it from sticking to the pan.
Adjust the amount of red chilli powder to suit your desired level of spiciness.
Rest the curry for 10-15 minutes off the heat before serving — the flavors continue to develop and deepen as it sits.

searchHistory.name: Chicken Curry
searchHistory.nutrition: Rich in vitamins, minerals and fiber. Provides sustained energy and supports digestion.
searchHistory.pairing: Serve with steamed rice or hot chapati
process: Wash and cut the chicken into medium sized pieces.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a deep kadai on medium flame.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, 2 dried red chillies and a pinch of hing (asafoetida).
Add 1 large finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until golden brown.
Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 2 minutes until raw smell goes away.
Add the chicken pieces, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and salt.
Mix well, add 1 cup water, cover and cook on low flame for 15-20 minutes.
Add 1/2 tsp garam masala, stir well and cook for 2 more minutes.
Turn off the stove. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot with rice.
tips: Cook on medium heat to avoid burning spices
Use fresh vegetables for best flavor
Adjust chilli powder to your spice tolerance

searchHistory.benefits: Contains antioxidants from spices like turmeric and cumin. Supports immunity and healthy metabolism.
searchHistory.name: Chicken Fry
searchHistory.nutrition: Rich in vitamins, minerals and fiber. Provides sustained energy and supports digestion.
searchHistory.pairing: Serve with steamed rice or hot chapati
process: Wash and chop the chicken into thin slices or small pieces.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a flat tawa or iron pan on medium-high flame.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and wait for them to crackle.
Add 8-10 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies, sauté for 30 seconds.
Add 1 medium sliced onion and fry for 4-5 minutes until edges turn brown.
Add the chicken slices, spread evenly in the pan.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, and salt to taste.
Cook on medium flame for 10-12 minutes, flipping occasionally for even crispiness.
Increase flame to high for last 2 minutes to get crispy edges.
Switch off stove. Squeeze half a lemon and garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot.
tips: Cook on medium heat to avoid burning spices
Use fresh vegetables for best flavor
Adjust chilli powder to your spice tolerance

searchHistory.name: Chicken Masala
searchHistory.nutrition: Rich in vitamins, minerals and fiber. Provides sustained energy and supports digestion.
searchHistory.pairing: Serve with steamed rice or hot chapati
process: Clean and cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil + 1 tbsp ghee in a heavy bottom pan on medium flame.
Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 cloves, 1 small cinnamon stick and let them sizzle.
Add 2 medium finely chopped onions and cook for 8-10 minutes until deep golden.
Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and oil separates (5-7 min).
Add 1 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, salt to taste.
Add the chicken pieces and mix well with the masala. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup water, cover with lid and cook on low flame for 15 minutes until tender.
Add 1 tsp garam masala, mix gently. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with chapati.
tips: Cook on medium heat to avoid burning spices
Use fresh vegetables for best flavor
Adjust chilli powder to your spice tolerance

favorites.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
favorites.nutrition:
Calories: ~420 kcal
Protein: 37g
Carbohydrates: 20g
Fat: 24g
Fiber: 4g
Sodium: 450mg
favorites.pairing: This dish is typically served with basmati rice or naan bread, and can be paired with a side of raita or a salad. For a more authentic experience, serve with a side of papadum or pickles. A glass of mango lassi or a cup of chai can complement the flavors of the dish.
process: Marinate the chicken breast in a mixture of 1/2 teaspoon garam masala powder, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1/4 teaspoon red chili powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt for at least 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the marinated chicken breast for 6-7 minutes per side, or until it is cooked through.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside.
In the same pan, add another tablespoon of vegetable oil and sauté 1 medium onion, chopped, until it is translucent.
Add 2 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute.
Add 1 medium tomato, chopped, and cook until it is soft.

Add 1 teaspoon of garam masala powder, 1 teaspoon of cumin powder, 1 teaspoon of coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon of red chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add 2 tablespoons of tomato puree, 2 tablespoons of water, and 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. Stir well.
Add the cooked chicken back into the pan and stir to coat with the sauce.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the chicken in the sauce for 10-12 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.
tips: Use high-quality spices to get the best flavor out of the dish.
Marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes to get the best flavor.
Use a mixture of tomato puree and water to get the right consistency of the sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro to add a fresh flavor to the dish.
